title: CRISPR-Cas9 Mutagenesis in Phaeodactylum tricornutum via Particle Bombardment
author: Mark Moosburner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7xqhpmw
materials: Plate wild-type Phaeodactylum in preparation for particle bombardment
Grow cells on plate for 4 days

Prepare particle bombardment materials - Turn on helium tank to pressure = 200psi - Obtain vacuum pump and set up with PDS-1000 - Re-suspend tungsten beads in 50% glycerol (vortex to mix) - Obtain a plat-form vortex - Prepare 2.5M CaCl 2 - Prepare 0.1M Spermidine - Prepare 70% EtOH - Obtain 100% EtOH - Obtain Isopropanol - 1 rupture disk - 7 macrocarrier disks - Place Phaeodactylum plate in PCR with the PDS-1000 system to allow the plate to dry before bombardment

steps.title: Calculate cell volume and pellet
steps.instruction: Calculate the concentration of the axenic Phaeodactylum tricornutum culture, determine the volume needed for 1 × 10⁸ cells, transfer that volume to a tube and pellet at 2000 × g for 20 min at 17 °C.

steps.title: Dry agar plate for spreading
steps.instruction: While cells are pelleting, dry a growth agar plate under a PCR hood. The plate contains 15 mL 1.6 % agarose mixed with 15 mL NO₃‑ASW (artificial seawater).

steps.title: Resuspend cells and spread
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cell pellet in 200 µL ASW, spread the suspension evenly on the dried agar plate, allow the cells to dry completely under the PCR hood, and seal the plate with breath‑easy tape.

steps.title: Prepare Cas9 and sgRNA plasmids
steps.instruction: Two days before bombardment, retrieve sequence‑verified Cas9 and sgRNA expression plasmids from frozen bacterial stocks, inoculate 15 mL of culture for each plasmid, and grow overnight (OVN).

steps.title: Mini‑prep and pool plasmids
steps.instruction: The next day, perform three 5 mL mini‑prep columns for each 15 mL culture and elute the three columns belonging to the same plasmid into a single 1.5 mL eppendorf.

steps.title: Quantify and concentrate DNA
steps.instruction: Measure plasmid concentration, calculate the volume that provides 8 µg of DNA for each plasmid, pipette 8 µg of each plasmid into a 1.5 mL eppendorf, and concentrate the combined DNA in a speed‑vac to a final volume of 5–10 µL.

steps.title: Prepare beads and sterilize disks
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL tungsten beads to the DNA‑containing tube and vortex for 5 min. Simultaneously sterilize the seven macrocarrier disks by pouring 70 % ethanol into a petri dish, shaking each disk in the ethanol with tweezers, and drying the disks on the opposite half of the dish.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL tungsten beads into the DNA tube.
Sterilize macrocarrier disks: pour 70 % EtOH into a petri dish, shake each disk in EtOH with tweezers, dry disks on the other half of the dish.

steps.title: Hybridize DNA to beads
steps.instruction: To the bead‑DNA mixture add 50 µL 2.5 M CaCl₂, vortex briefly, then add 20 µL 0.1 M spermidine, flick the tube repeatedly to promote hybridization, and vortex the mixture for an additional 3 minutes.

steps.title: Wash and ethanol‑resuspend beads
steps.instruction: Pellet the bead‑DNA mixture in a tabletop centrifuge at 8000 rpm for 10 seconds, discard the supernatant, resuspend in 140 µL 100 % ethanol and mix thoroughly by pipetting; repeat the pelleting and resuspension two more times, and on the final resuspension add only 100 µL 100 % ethanol, mix thoroughly and maintain homogeneity by flicking the tube.

steps.title: Load beads onto macrocarrier disks
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL of the washed bead suspension onto each of the seven macrocarrier disks, allow the beads to dry completely, then place the disks into the carrier‑disk manifold, ensuring each disk is secured under its lip.

steps.title: Assemble bombardment apparatus
steps.instruction: Briefly wash a rupture disk in isopropanol, insert the wet rupture disk into the rupture manifold and screw the manifold into the bombardment system, secure the metal mesh screen between the two plates of the carrier‑disk manifold, and insert the carrier‑disk manifold into the square metal fitting directly above the seven holes of the rupture manifold.

substeps.instruction: Insert wet rupture disk into rupture manifold and screw into system.
Secure metal mesh screen between carrier‑disk plates.
Insert carrier‑disk manifold into square metal fitting aligned with the seven holes.

steps.title: Position plate and fire
steps.instruction: Place the prepared Phaeodactylum plate beneath the carrier‑disk manifold, close the bombardment chamber door, turn on the vacuum manifold and let the pressure rise to 25 in Hg, then press and hold the “FIRE” button until the pressure reaches ~1300 psi and the rupture disk bursts (audible bang); immediately vent the system to release the vacuum.

steps.title: Incubate bombarded plate
steps.instruction: Replace the plate lid, wrap the plate in tin foil, and incubate at 18 °C for 48 hours in the dark.

steps.title: Harvest cells after incubation
steps.instruction: After 48 hours, scrape the cells from the plate and resuspend them in 2 mL ASW in a 2 mL eppendorf.

steps.title: Prepare selection agar plates
steps.instruction: Mix 15 mL 1.6 % agarose, 15 mL ASW containing the appropriate nitrogen substrate, and Phleomycin at 20 mg/mL; pour into plates and dry them under a PCR hood before use.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells on selection media
steps.instruction: For each transformation, dry three selection plates, spread up to 400 µL of the resuspended cells onto each plate, allow the spots to dry completely under the PCR hood, and incubate; Phleomycin‑resistant colonies become visible after 3–4 weeks.
